The scheme theoretic image of <MATH_0001> is constructed in Section
<REF_0001>. Since <MATH_0002> is quasi-compact
(Lemma <REF_0002>)
we find that <MATH_0003> is quasi-compact
(Schemes, Lemma <REF_0003>).
Hence <MATH_0004>
is dense (Lemma <REF_0004>).
On the other hand <MATH_0005> is closed in <MATH_0006>
(Lemma <REF_0005>)
hence <MATH_0007> is surjective.
Thus <MATH_0008> is a proper (Lemma <REF_0006>).

<STRUCT_0001>
The target of a separated scheme under a surjective
universally closed morphism is separated.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a surjective universally closed
morphism of schemes over <MATH_0003>.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0004> is quasi-separated, then <MATH_0005> is quasi-separated.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0006> is separated, then <MATH_0007> is separated.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0008> is quasi-separated over <MATH_0009>, then <MATH_0010> is quasi-separated over <MATH_0011>.
<STRUCT_0005> If <MATH_0012> is separated over <MATH_0013>, then <MATH_0014> is separated over <MATH_0015>.
<STRUCT_0006>

Parts (1) and (2) are a consequence of (3) and (4) for
<MATH_0001> (see
Schemes, Definition <REF_0001>).
Consider the commutative diagram
<MATH_0002>
The left vertical arrow is surjective (i.e., universally surjective).
The right vertical arrow is universally closed as a composition
of the universally closed morphisms
<MATH_0003>. Hence it is also
quasi-compact, see
Lemma <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume <MATH_0004> is quasi-separated over <MATH_0005>, i.e.,  <MATH_0006> is
quasi-compact. If <MATH_0007> is a quasi-compact
open, then <MATH_0008>
is surjective and <MATH_0009> is quasi-compact by our remarks
above. We conclude that <MATH_0010> is quasi-compact, i.e., <MATH_0011>
is quasi-separated over <MATH_0012>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Assume <MATH_0013> is separated over <MATH_0014>, i.e., <MATH_0015> is a closed
immersion. Then <MATH_0016> is closed as a
composition of closed morphisms. Since <MATH_0017> is
surjective, it follows that <MATH_0018> is closed in <MATH_0019>.
Hence <MATH_0020> is separated over <MATH_0021> by the discussion following
Schemes, Definition <REF_0003>.
